TX-2025892-SB8.aiSummary: Texas SB 8 would require certain state and local buildings to set shared restrooms, locker rooms, changing rooms, and showers for use by one sex only, with some exceptions for care, repairs, emergencies, young children, and similar needs. It would also require inmates to be housed by sex and limit some female-only family violence shelters to female victims and their children. If a state or local body violates the law, it could face fines, and affected people or the attorney general could sue to enforce it.

TX-2025892-HB18.aiSummary: The law limits certain campaign donations and spending for lawmakers and some political committees during a member’s unexcused absence from a legislative session. It bars accepting donations above a set daily amount and spending on travel, food, or lodging tied to that absence, and it can lead to a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for each violation. It takes effect 91 days after the last day of the legislative session and applies to covered donations or spending on or after that date.

TX-2025892-HB1.aiSummary: This law changes rules for youth camps in Texas. It requires camp emergency plans, safety training, weather alerts, backup internet, and some notice to parents and local officials. It also sets rules for inspections and can lead to license denial or suspension if a camp does not follow the new requirements.
